name: me.chargingnear/mcp
title: ChargingNear.me
description: U.S. EV chargers: nearby, routes, stats, highway gaps, NEVI, trucks, Supercharger pipeline, my saves

tools.name: search_stations
tools.description: Chargers in a city or state, filtered the way drivers ask: "Electrify America chargers in Phoenix", "CHAdeMO chargers in Seattle", "150 kW chargers in Denver". Filters: city, state, network, connector (NACS/Tesla, CCS, CHAdeMO, J1772), speed, min_power_kw and live availability. Each station comes with its address, network, connector types, power in kW, port counts, access hours, price where known, the date its details were last confirmed and its page link (url); results are sorted by station name.

city.description: City name, e.g. Denver (with state for a common name)

state.description: State: two-letter abbreviation (CO), name (Colorado) or slug (colorado)

network.description: Network name contains, e.g. Tesla, Electrify America, ChargePoint

connector.description: Plug type, case-insensitive: NACS (Tesla), CCS, CHAdeMO or J1772, or a raw NREL code (TESLA, J1772COMBO, CHADEMO). Comma-separate to match any.

speed.description: Charging level: dcfc (DC fast), level2 or level1

min_power_kw.description: Minimum charger power in kW (e.g. 50, 150, 250). 150 and up only match stations with a known wattage.

available_now.description: Only stations showing a free port in a live reading under 15 minutes old. Live availability is available only to clients with a commercial API key; without one, this filter is ignored and the answer lists it under ignored_filters.

tools.name: get_nearest_stations
tools.description: Chargers near a place or point: "EV chargers near Boulder", "fast chargers near Union Station, Denver", "Tesla/NACS chargers near me" (with the driver's city, ZIP code or coordinates), "is there a working charger at the Costco in Fort Collins?". Send place (a U.S. city, address, ZIP code, landmark or business name) or lat and lng; optional speed (dcfc = DC fast), min_power_kw, connector, network and radius. Lists in-service stations only (removed and temporarily closed ones are left out). Each station comes with its distance in miles, network, connector types, power in kW, DC fast and Level 2 port counts, price where known, the date its details were last confirmed and its ChargingNear.me page link (url), plus live port availability where a live reading exists (included for clients with a commercial API key). Results are sorted by distance, nearest first. With place, the answer's place field names the match.

place.description: A U.S. city, address, ZIP code, landmark or business name, e.g. "Union Station, Denver, CO" or "80202". Use instead of lat and lng; sent with them, the match nearest that point is used.

lat.description: Latitude (with lng), if you have coordinates instead of a place

connector.description: Plug type, case-insensitive: NACS (Tesla), CCS, CHAdeMO or J1772, or a raw NREL code (TESLA, J1772COMBO, CHADEMO). Comma-separate to match any.

network.description: Network name contains, e.g. Tesla, Electrify America, ChargePoint

speed.description: Charging level: dcfc (DC fast), level2 or level1

min_power_kw.description: Minimum charger power in kW (e.g. 50, 150, 250). 150 and up only match stations with a known wattage.

available_now.description: Only stations showing a free port in a live reading under 15 minutes old. Live availability is available only to clients with a commercial API key; without one, this filter is ignored and the answer lists it under ignored_filters.

tools.name: get_station_details
tools.description: One station in full: "is that charger open 24 hours?", "which plugs and prices does it have?", "is it still in service?". Send id, the station number from get_nearest_stations, search_stations or find_stations_on_route. Answers with name, address, network, connector types, power in kW, port counts, access hours, price where known, the date its details were last confirmed and its page link (url), plus live port availability where a live reading exists (included for clients with a commercial API key). A removed or temporarily closed station answers with its status instead.

id.description: Station ID, the id field of a station in another tool's answer

tools.name: get_city_charging_stats
tools.description: Charging in one U.S. city: "how many chargers does Austin have?", "which networks run the chargers in Chicago?". Send city and state ("Los Angeles" and "CA" or "California"), or slug: the city and state in one line ("Los Angeles, CA") or the city slug (los-angeles-ca). Answers with the city's station count, DC fast and Level 2 counts, top networks and the city page link (url). A city name alone picks the city of that name with the most stations and lists the others under other_matches.

state.description: The city's state: two-letter code (CO) or name (Colorado)

slug.description: Instead of city and state: "Los Angeles, CA" or the city slug (los-angeles-ca)

tools.name: get_state_charging_stats
tools.description: Charging in one U.S. state: "how many EV chargers are in Colorado?", "which networks have the most chargers in Florida?". Send state: a two-letter code (CO), name (Colorado) or slug (colorado). Answers with the state's station count, DC fast and Level 2 counts, number of cities with charging, top networks and the state page link (url).

state.description: State: two-letter code (CO), name (Colorado) or slug (colorado)

slug.description: Same as state (kept for older calls)

tools.name: get_catalog_totals
tools.description: Nationwide numbers: "how many public EV charging locations are in the U.S.?". The size of the ChargingNear.me U.S. catalog, computed live: charging locations (physical sites; every charger at one address counts once), ports (plugs; each charges one car at a time), DC fast ports, states covered and networks. The summary field is the same sentence the website shows.

tools.name: find_stations_on_route
tools.description: Chargers on a drive: "fast chargers on my drive from Denver to Salt Lake City", "where can I charge between Chicago and Omaha?", "Tesla chargers on I-80 from Reno to Sacramento". Send from and to (U.S. place names, or "lat,lng"), with via for stops in between; or waypoints in driving order, each {place} or {lat, lng} (2 to 10 places, or up to 100 points: add one every 50 to 100 miles). With place names the route follows roads and each station gets route_mile, its miles from the start. Optional speed (dcfc for long drives), min_power_kw, connector, network and corridor_miles. Each station comes with its network, connector types, power in kW, DC fast and Level 2 port counts, price where known, the date its details were last confirmed and its ChargingNear.me page link (url), plus live port availability where a live reading exists (included for clients with a commercial API key). With place names, results are sorted by route_mile; with points, by segment in driving order, then by distance from the segment's midpoint.

from.description: Where the drive starts: a U.S. city, address or business name ("Denver, CO"), or "lat,lng"

to.description: Where the drive ends, like from ("Salt Lake City, UT")

via.description: Stops in between, in driving order, like from (optional)

waypoints.description: Instead of from and to: every stop in driving order, each {place} or {lat, lng}

place.description: A U.S. city, address or business name, e.g. "Denver, CO"

corridor_miles.description: Width of search corridor in miles from route (default 5, max 25)

limit_per_waypoint.description: Max stations per waypoint segment (default 5, max 10)

connector.description: Plug type, case-insensitive: NACS (Tesla), CCS, CHAdeMO or J1772, or a raw NREL code (TESLA, J1772COMBO, CHADEMO). Comma-separate to match any.

network.description: Network name contains, e.g. Tesla, Electrify America, ChargePoint

speed.description: Charging level: dcfc (DC fast), level2 or level1

min_power_kw.description: Minimum charger power in kW (e.g. 50, 150, 250). 150 and up only match stations with a known wattage.

available_now.description: Only stations showing a free port in a live reading under 15 minutes old. Live availability is available only to clients with a commercial API key; without one, this filter is ignored and the answer lists it under ignored_filters.

tools.name: get_charging_gaps
tools.description: Charging gaps on highways: "charging gaps on I-80", "where can't I fast charge on I-90 in Montana?". Stretches over 50 miles of U.S. Interstates, U.S. highways and designated EV Alternative Fuel Corridors with no fast charger within 5 miles of the highway, measured in a straight line (measure "practical", the default, longest first). With measure "nevi": stretches with no fast charger within 1 mile of the highway (the federal NEVI siting distance), by state and highway, each listing the fast chargers 1 to 5 miles off with name, city, network, fast ports, plugs, miles off and nearest mile marker. Filter by state, highway and length. From our daily open-data files (CC BY 4.0); each answer carries the file's version, date, definition and cite_as line.

measure.description: practical: no fast charger within 5 miles of the highway, measured in a straight line (the headline measure). nevi: no fast charger within 1 mile of the highway (the federal NEVI siting distance), with the chargers 1 to 5 miles off each stretch.

highway.description: Highway as signed, e.g. I-70, US-40, CO-82

min_miles.description: Only gaps at least this long, in miles

designated.description: true: only gaps on FHWA-designated Alternative Fuel Corridors; false: only undesignated ones

tools.name: get_corridor_chargers
tools.description: Fast chargers along a Colorado highway: "every fast charger on I-70 from Denver to Grand Junction", "the longest gap on US-285". Every DC fast charging location on a corridor, in driving order, with mile points, distance from the previous charger, ports and power, plus the corridor's longest gaps and how many miles meet the NEVI 50-mile rule. Colorado corridors: I-70, Denver to Grand Junction; I-25, Wyoming to New Mexico; I-76, Denver to the Nebraska Line; US-285, Denver to the New Mexico Line; CO-82, Glenwood Springs to Aspen; US-40, I-70 to Steamboat Springs.

tools.name: get_nevi_status
tools.description: Federal NEVI compliance: "which fast chargers in Colorado meet NEVI?", "why do stations near I-95 fail NEVI?". Which open public DC fast stations meet the federal NEVI minimums (four CCS ports at 150 kW, within 1 mile of a designated corridor), with the reason each one fails, a pass/fail count, and corridor coverage of the 50-mile rule for a state or highway. The rule and its dated sources come with every answer.

grade.description: Only passing or only failing stations

network.description: Network name contains, e.g. Electrify America

tools.name: find_truck_charging
tools.description: Electric truck charging and Tesla Megachargers: "Tesla Megacharger locations", "truck charging near Waco, TX", "Megachargers in Texas", "MCS chargers on my drive from Atlanta to Savannah", "where is the next Megacharger opening?". Tesla's public Megacharger sites (for Tesla Semi) and other networks' heavy-duty truck sites, including megawatt (MCS, SAE J3271) sites from NREL. Send place (or lat and lng) for the nearest sites, sorted by distance, nearest first; state for one state's sites; or from and to (with optional via) for sites along a drive, sorted by miles from the start. With none of these, every site is listed, open ones first. Filter by status (open, construction, permit, announced or not_open) and kind (megacharger, other_networks or mcs). Each site comes with its status, stalls and power per stall where published, connector, host, access, address (the town only where the street address isn't published yet), last-verified date, every source with its link and date, and its ChargingNear.me page link (url). A site is Open only when Tesla or its host confirms it; a permit filing doesn't make it Open.

place.description: A U.S. city, address, ZIP code or truck stop, e.g. "Waco, TX", for the nearest sites. Use instead of lat and lng.

lat.description: Latitude (with lng), if you have coordinates instead of a place

state.description: Only one state's sites: a two-letter code (TX) or name (Texas)

from.description: For sites along a drive: where it starts, a U.S. city or address ("Atlanta, GA"), or "lat,lng"

to.description: Where the drive ends, like from ("Savannah, GA")

via.description: Stops in between, in driving order, like from (optional)

status.description: open; construction (under construction); permit (permit filed); announced; not_open (every site not open yet); any (the default)

kind.description: megacharger: Tesla Megachargers; other_networks: other networks' heavy-duty truck sites; mcs: sites with MCS (SAE J3271) plugs; all (the default)

radius.description: With place or lat and lng: only sites within this many miles (max 3000; by default the nearest sites at any distance)

corridor_miles.description: With from and to: how far from the route a site may be, in miles (default 10, max 25)

tools.name: find_supercharger_pipeline
tools.description: Tesla Superchargers that are planned, permit filed, under construction or newly opened in the U.S.: "Tesla Superchargers coming soon near Austin", "Superchargers under construction in Ohio", "new Tesla Superchargers this month", "third-party Superchargers". Site data from supercharge.info, read twice a day. Send place (or lat and lng) for the nearest sites, nearest first; state for one state's sites; stage to choose pipeline (the default: planned, permit filed and under construction), planned, permit, construction, opened (opened in the last 30 days), vote (sites in Tesla's location vote) or any. Filter by third_party (sites a third party owns), open_to_other_evs and nevi_funded. Each site comes with its status and the day it started, its source link, stalls, power, plugs, whether other EVs can charge, host, address or town, third-party owner, NEVI match, its ChargingNear.me page (url) and, once open, its station page (station_url). No pipeline site has a published opening date.

place.description: A U.S. city, address or ZIP code, e.g. "Austin, TX", for the nearest sites. Use instead of lat and lng.

lat.description: Latitude (with lng), if you have coordinates instead of a place

state.description: Only one state's sites: a two-letter code (OH) or name (Ohio)

stage.description: pipeline (planned, permit filed and under construction; the default); planned; permit; construction; opened (opened in the last 30 days); vote (in Tesla's location vote); any

third_party.description: true: only sites a third party owns (not Tesla); false: only Tesla's own

open_to_other_evs.description: true: only sites supercharge.info lists as open to other EVs

nevi_funded.description: true: only sites our NEVI data matches by location (150 m)

radius.description: With place or lat and lng: only sites within this many miles (max 3000; by default the nearest at any distance)

tools.name: get_my_saved_stations
tools.description: "Which chargers have I saved?": the charging stations the signed-in driver saved on ChargingNear.me, newest first: name, network, city, state, DC fast and Level 2 port counts, their note and the station page link. Needs the driver to sign in to ChargingNear.me; without sign-in it answers with a short message and the sign-in page link.

tools.name: get_my_trips
tools.description: "What road trips have I saved?": the trips the signed-in driver saved on ChargingNear.me, newest first: start, destination, distance, driving time, the charging stops in driving order (name, network, city, state, station page link) and the trip page link. Needs the driver to sign in to ChargingNear.me; without sign-in it answers with a short message and the sign-in page link.

tools.name: get_my_alerts
tools.description: "Which charging alerts do I have?": the alerts the signed-in driver set up on ChargingNear.me: stations watched for a free charger, price alerts on stations and saved trips, network status alerts and alert areas, each with what triggers it, whether it is on and when it last sent. Needs the driver to sign in to ChargingNear.me; without sign-in it answers with a short message and the sign-in page link.
